kill.text: Price below $450 (pre-split basis; halve this level after the 19 Jan 2027 Class C dividend)
Street mean target below $650 (pre-split basis; halve after 19 Jan 2027)
Revenue growth below 15% for two quarters while capex keeps rising
Further legal settlements above $10B or a ruling forcing divestiture of Instagram/WhatsApp
2027 capex guide implies negative full-year free cash flow

tam.market: Global digital advertising (social, messaging, AI assistants)
tam.source: Global digital advertising ~$1.0T in 2026 (Google ~$300B and Meta ~$258B annualised alone), ValueInvestor estimate ~$1.5T by 2031 (~8-9% a year) and ~$2.2T by 2036 (in line with the ~$2.19T-by-2035 forecast reported by Communicate Online).
tam.why_share: Meta takes ~26% of global digital ads today (~$258B of ~$1T); we assume 24% then 22% as AI assistants and TikTok compete.
tam.what_must_go_right: AI ranking keeps lifting ad prices; WhatsApp business messaging scales; net margin recovers to ~35% after the capex peak. Figures are pre-Class C dividend (halve per-share values after 19 Jan 2027).

scenarios.note: Implies ~$360B revenue in 2031 (~7% a year from 2026's ~$258B); pre-split share count.
Reality Labs and AI glasses are excluded (option value).

sections.industry_map: Meta owns Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger and Threads (3.64B daily users), sells ads across them, and spends on AI (Meta Superintelligence Labs, Llama/Muse) and Reality Labs (glasses, VR).
sections.size_growth: Digital ads ~$750B growing ~10%; Meta is growing far faster: Q3 2026 revenue $64.6B (+26%), ad impressions +10%, price per ad +14% (Meta Q3 release, 21 Oct 2026). Ads are cyclical with consumer spend.
sections.structure: Social ads duopoly with Google in the US plus TikTok; strong network effects; regulation (privacy, child safety) is the main barrier and risk.
sections.demand_supply: Advertiser demand strong as AI targeting improves returns; Meta's own compute need is the bottleneck. 2026 capex $135-145B; 2027 will be higher (no number yet).
sections.industry_risks: (1) Legal and regulatory - high probability, medium impact: an August 2026 settlement with 52 state attorneys general costs up to ~$18.6B ($9.9B charged in Q3); warning: new suits. (2) AI capex overbuild - medium/high. (3) Ad cycle downturn - low-medium/medium. (4) TikTok resurgence - low/medium.
sections.outlook: Near: revenue growth mid-20s%, FCF near zero as capex ramps (Q3 FCF -$2.1B), no buybacks in 2026. Mid: AI-driven ad gains and messaging monetisation (WhatsApp) keep growth high-teens. Long: AI assistants and glasses as a new platform are options.
sections.winners: Engagement scale, ad-ranking AI, compute capacity, ability to self-fund, regulatory management.
sections.business: Family of Apps produces all profit; Reality Labs loses $18-19B in 2026 (narrowing to ~$15B in 2027). Q3 operating income $13B (20% margin) including the $9.9B legal charge; excluding it ~$22.9B (35%), EPS $7.40.
sections.right_to_win: No other company has 3.6B daily users plus a frontier-scale AI effort and a direct-response ad engine; better AI ranking turns straight into higher ad prices.
sections.moat: Wide: network effects and data scale. Trend: stable; AI improves monetisation, regulation chips at the edges.
sections.tam_competitors: ~20%+ of global digital ads. Competitors: Google, TikTok, Amazon ads, AppLovin. Runway: WhatsApp business messaging, AI agents for businesses, Threads ads.
sections.management: Founder-CEO Mark Zuckerberg controls voting; bold capital allocator (Reality Labs, AI) with a record of both waste and huge wins. Headcount down 15% year on year. Buybacks paused in 2026 to fund capex; dividend continues. A non-voting Class C share dividend on 19 Jan 2027 will halve the Class A price (works like a 2-for-1 split).
sections.financials: Revenue $86B (2020) to $201B (2025), operating margin 25-42%, ROIC 19-34%. FCF $46B in 2025, falling in 2026 ($11B for nine months). Long-term debt up to $80.9B from $58.7B; cash $82.5B. EPS 2025 $23.49; nine-month 2026 EPS $20.44.
sections.company_risks: (1) Capex payback - KPI: revenue growth vs expense growth (expenses +68% in Q3 including the charge). (2) Legal - KPI: settlements. (3) Engagement - KPI: daily users (+3%). (4) Reality Labs burn - KPI: losses above $20B.
sections.variant_view: The market sees Meta as an AI spender with legal overhangs; we believe its ad engine is compounding at 25%+ with AI-driven price gains, so ex-charge earnings power (~$30/share) makes it cheaper than it looks at ~20x.
sections.valuation: Our value (owner earnings $30/share, 11% then 8%, 9.5% discount): low $480, base $785, high $1,050; price $610 implies ~16% growth vs 18% history. Street mean $850 (57 analysts). Peers: ~20x ex-charge EPS vs GOOGL ~24x. Required margin of safety 25% gives entry $589, 3% below today. All figures are pre-Class C dividend; halve them after 19 Jan 2027. Ming does not have a recorded position yet; add shares and cost in the app.
sections.pillars: (1) Revenue growth above 18% - breach: below 15% for two quarters. (2) Ex-charge operating margin above 35% - breach below 30%. (3) Capex returns visible as ad price gains - breach: price per ad flat while capex rises. (4) No structural break-up - breach: ruling forcing divestiture.
sections.catalysts_flow: Q4 results (late Jan 2027) with 2027 capex and expense guide; Class C dividend 19 Jan 2027; Muse/AI assistant monetisation updates. Sellers: funds trimming on capex and legal news (stock fell ~7-9% after Q3). Buyers: GARP funds at ~20x.
sections.premortem: (1) 2027 capex guide shocks and FCF goes negative for years. (2) A youth-safety ruling or settlement wave far larger than $18.6B. (3) AI assistants shift attention away from feeds.
